seoDescription: Drone control in fabric: IMU fusion, a fixed-point rate loop and PWM generation with deterministic latency from sample to actuator.

sections.heading: Codex of the Swarm
sections.body: on the flight of many machines, and how they keep from striking one another

images.caption: Fig. A — the aerial screw. One rotor lifts one machine; this codex concerns many.

sections.body: A ROS 2 and PX4 SITL multi-drone swarm package. It spans single-drone offboard control through to decentralised formation flight, area-coverage missions, collision avoidance and leader-failure reassignment, all driven from a single YAML config and one ros2 launch invocation. It speaks to PX4 through uXRCE-DDS and px4_msgs, not MAVROS.
sections.kicker: Every result below is simulated, in Gazebo Harmonic 8.11.0 with PX4 SITL. No real-hardware flight has ever been performed. Where the README and the claims matrix disagree, the matrix is right.

sections.heading: Of Formation and Order
sections.body:
Three machines rise in a triangle: one leader at the origin, two followers set three paces behind and three to either side. The leader walks its path fifteen metres out and back at five metres' height; the followers keep station in its frame.

Should the leader fall silent, each follower names the lowest-numbered peer still speaking. Every drone reaches the same answer from its own view, and no council is needed.
INIT → ARM_OFFBOARD → FLY → LAND → DONE. Arming waits for 25 ticks of stable OFFBOARD.
Fig. B — spawns from config/formation.yaml. Dashed rings mark MIN_DIST_SOFT, 1.5 m.

sections.heading: Of Near Collisions
sections.body: Three layers keep the machines apart: a clamp holding each setpoint 2.5 m from any peer, a quadratic repulsive velocity up to 4 m/s inside 1.5 m, and a full halt below 0.6 m. Across 98 nights, from 18 May to 24 August 2026, ten fault scenarios were injected and every surviving log re-parsed.

sections.heading: Fig. C — Worst Separation by Scenario
Fig. D — Runs Below the Hard Floor (1.0 m)
The Flaw, Honestly Kept
sections.body:
64 of 2,852 completed runs fell below 1.5 m and 37 below 1.0 m; the worst came within 0.22 m. 33 of the 37 hard-floor breaches sit in two scenarios, dds_loss_5 and dds_delay_50.

All three layers read peer position. Degrade the transport and the clamp clamps against stale data, repulsion pushes from a phantom, and the halt never arms.

sections.heading: What Held
sections.body: Under CPU stress at two cores, 441 runs recorded 0 violations with a worst separation of 1.52 m. Leader and follower kills recovered through decentralised reassignment.
sections.kicker: 2,003 runs died before their completion line and are not counted in the figures.
